reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of BayesBlend lies in its formalization of Bayesian stacking as a convex optimization problem over posterior predictive densities. The pseudo-BMA approach approximates Bayesian model averaging using PSIS-LOO, offering computational tractability while preserving predictive accuracy. Complete-pooling stacking optimizes weights globally, assuming equal contribution from all models. In contrast, hierarchical stacking introduces a soft-max regression framework where weights depend on observed covariates such as game state or player performance metrics. This allows for dynamic adaptation of model weights over time, crucial for real-time sports prediction. The failure mode of pseudo-BMA occurs when model fits are too disparate or when PSIS-LOO becomes unstable. Complete-pooling stacking may overfit if models are highly correlated or mis-specified. Hierarchical stacking requires sufficient data to estimate the regression parameters reliably. These primitives form a layered architecture for ensemble learning in GSI and GSE, supporting both static and adaptive model blending strategies.
